promise: Helion planned to bring its first fusion power plant online by 2028, targeting at least 50 MW after a one-year ramp-up.
description: Helion announced a power-purchase agreement with Microsoft on May 10, 2023. The 2028 target concerns bringing the plant online; the stated generating-capacity target follows a one-year ramp-up.
evidence: Helion's announcement distinguishes the online date from the subsequent capacity target.
Outcome not established as of 2026-09-21: the checked announcement does not demonstrate commercial power delivery; the online target remains future.

promise: AI will surpass "almost all humans at almost everything" shortly after 2027
description: At Davos in January 2025, Amodei forecast broad AI capability within a few years. The forecast was uncertain and did not define a test for completion.
evidence: Amodei: milestone expected 'shortly after 2027', exact timing uncertain
Milestone not publicly demonstrated as of mid-2026

review.note: A probabilistic forecast is not a delivery pledge. No measurable universal test or literal December 2028 cutoff is established.

promise: Implement the EWENE Acceleration Plan 2026-2028 with KSh7.5 billion for maternal, newborn and reproductive health
description: Ruto launched the programme on May 28, 2026. The announced funding comprises KSh4 billion through the Social Health Authority, KSh1 billion for essential commodities and KSh2.5 billion for family-planning supplies.
evidence: Launch is documented; full programme financing and health outcomes over 2026-2028 remain to be established.

promise: Intend to pledge EUR 700 million to the Global Fund's eighth replenishment for 2026-2028, subject to EU budget availability
description: The Commission announced the intended pledge at the One Health Summit on April 7, 2026. EUR 185 million was available under the current financial framework; the remainder depends on future budget provision.
evidence: The Global Fund's donor profile, updated August 12, 2026, recorded EUR 700 million pledged and no contributions yet for this replenishment.

promise: Establish compute-financing partnerships aiming to mobilize more than USD 500 billion of third-party capital over time
description: NVIDIA announced MOUs with six financial institutions on August 10, 2026. The contemplated financing is third-party capital, and NVIDIA's potential backstop is optional.
evidence: The company announcement and Reuters report establish the partnerships but no completion timetable.

review.note: Announcement and prospective financing scale are supported. Reuters explicitly says no deployment timetable was disclosed; December 2028 is an editorial horizon. MOUs and an optional backstop do not guarantee fundraising.
